author: Leanne Sanders
title: First Nations advocate finds lack of coordinated response to B.C.’s raging wildfires ‘gobsmacking’
content:
Cindy Blackstock is raising concerns after recently helping her brother evacuate a wildfire in the Lillooet area near Cache Creek, B.C. calling the lack of a coordinated response gobsmacking.


Blackstock is from the Gitxsan First Nation and now lives in Tk̓emlúps te Secwépemc territory, but grew up around fire stations in northern B.C. Last week, she and a sister came to the aid of her brother whose home was under threat.


“On my brother’s house cameras, they were putting the hoses around his house and on the roof and everything else, but there was still no evacuation order,” Blackstock told

APTN News

.


“In his situation, there was a fire alert by the neighboring First Nation, a fire alert by the other regional district, but the one where he was in did not set it. And so it took some advocacy to get them to do that even though the fire was just over the other side of the mountain.”


Blackstock, who is a well-known First Nations child welfare advocate, said her father worked for the fire service when she was growing up and her brother followed in his footsteps working for the B.C. Forest service for decades.


“One of the things that just is gobsmacking to me is how many different jurisdictions there are when it comes to declaring fire alerts or evacuation orders…each one of them has independent authority to do these things along with each First Nation. It doesn’t appear to be the level of coordination that there should have been on this with my brother in the area he was in,” Blackstock said.


“When we were growing up in the bush, we knew the bush, knew fire behavior and everything else like this. But they’re not using that type of knowledge that they should be using to help, first of all, deal with drought conditions, which is severe drought underlying that. Number two is, to really understand the land and the landscape and get these fires under control at their earliest stages. I was so gobsmacked that it took them so long to declare a state of emergency when there were so many people evacuated. And frankly, there were so many vacationers in the Okanagan area.”


Blackstock said despite Hwy 97 being closed in both directions due to wildfires, there was no evacuation order. She was surprised to see a lot of vacationers travelling in the direction of the fire “clogging up” different areas.


They also encountered delays due to roadwork taking place with one lane closed, making for slow going not only for people leaving, but for frontline workers trying to access the area.


“There were fire trucks and emergency vehicles that were in the lineup while they’re doing paving,” Blackstock said. “When we were driving out, there [were] seniors and we stopped to talk to them. Because the only way that you get a fire alert in these regions is if you proactively go on to a website or app. This is an area where there isn’t tech service or that kind of thing. There’s some phone service. You’ve got email, basically and this Elder wasn’t even aware that there was a fire alert. And, so we were briefing her up and telling her that she should get out of there. Thankfully, she had younger family members with her to help her,” Blackstock said.


“And that’s the type of thing that’s happening on the ground. And I attribute that just to really lack of provincial coordination amongst the different jurisdictions.”


Residents leaving wildfire stricken areas near Cache Creek, BC encountered delays due to roadwork. Photo: Cindy Blackstock


Blackstock was also not impressed by what turned out to be the accommodations for frontline workers that she initially thought was a tent city. Describing their work as physically and mentally exhausting, Blackstock said it was far different from what firefighters were provided when she was young.


“We had Atco trailers and industrial sized tents for people and [we]made sure they were fed properly so that they could rest and recuperate and do their work…So it needs to be better coordination, and there definitely needs to be more resources on the front line to support these firefighters and to the state of emergency-there shouldn’t be things like paving roadworks on the lone stretch of highway that people are using to evacuate or the emergency personnel are using to access,” Blackstock said.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Docentes de Misiones iniciaron un nuevo paro docente de 48 horas
content:
El Frente de Trabajadores de la Educación en Lucha (FTEL) y el Movimiento Pedagógico de Liberación (MPL), junto a otros gremios disidentes, iniciaron este martes 11 de agosto de 2026 un paro docente de 48 horas sin asistencia a los lugares de trabajo en Misiones, con cortes de ruta y movilizaciones en reclamo de una nueva recomposición salarial.


Entre los reclamos se encuentran: el rechazo a los aumentos salariales otorgados por el gobierno provincial de Hugo Passalacqua por considerarlos insuficientes, la exigencia de una nueva convocatoria a mesa paritaria, exigencias por mejoras en infraestructura escolar y mayor presupuesto para comedores, y la solicitud de normalización de las prestaciones de la obra social provincial (IPS).


La secretaria general de la Unión de Docentes Nueva Argentina Misiones, Estela Genesini, en la asamblea provincial realizada esta mañana en la localidad de Jardín América, expresó: “Un docente gana 800 mil pesos, pero un diputado gana 10 millones. ¿Entienden la diferencia? Nosotros nos vamos a ir con el 82% si trabajamos 37 años de 800 mil pesos. ¿Ustedes saben lo que es eso? 560 mil pesos”.


Además, Genesini agregó: “Y los tipos se van con 7 o 8 millones, ¿entienden la diferencia? Más allá de la cantidad que somos, nosotros decimos que tenemos que ser esa llama encendida en cada localidad”.

author: Juanita León
title: A natureza dita a agenda do novo presidente da Colômbia
content:
O terremoto que matou pelo menos 169 colombianos e deixou mais de mil feridos em quase metade do país confirma uma velha máxima da política local: é a natureza que, muitas vezes, acaba ditando a agenda dos presidentes.


Por volta das 7h30 da manhã do dia 10 de agosto, um terremoto de magnitude 7,4 na Escala Richter atingiu San José del Palmar, cidade no departamento de Chocó, no oeste da Colômbia. O episódio se tornou o primeiro grande teste para o presidente Abelardo de la Espriella, que havia tomado posse apenas três dias antes.


Depois de uma cerimônia de posse marcada por símbolos, de um intenso debate sobre a “batalha cultural” que o novo presidente pretende travar e das primeiras demonstrações da política de linha dura que de la Espriella prometeu — com transferência de presos e operações militares —, o show acabou. Agora começa, de fato, a difícil tarefa de enfrentar os problemas concretos do país.


O que aconteceu


O tremor teve magnitude 7,4 e ocorreu a 96 quilômetros de profundidade, segundo o Serviço Geológico Colombiano (SGC). A intensidade foi semelhante à dos

dois terremotos registrados na Venezuela

 em 24 de junho, de magnitudes 7,2 e 7,5. A principal diferença foi a profundidade: os tremores no país vizinho foram mais superficiais e, por isso, provocaram mais danos.


O município de San José del Palmar (Chocó) foi o epicentro do terremoto. A cidade tem uma população de 5.809 habitantes e conta com apenas 32 milhões de pesos colombianos [cerca de 54.400 de reais] do fundo da Unidade Nacional de Gestão de Riscos,

segundo o prefeito León Fabio Marín

. “Somos um município muito pobre, com recursos escassos”, afirmou.


Até o momento, segundo relatos preliminares, nenhum morador de San José del Palmar morreu em decorrência do terremoto.

Marín, no entanto, relata que cerca de 400 moradias foram afetadas e que 20 estruturas desabaram completamente

.


O tremor foi sentido em 11 departamentos do país, isto é, praticamente todo o território nacional, especialmente em Bogotá, Medellín, Ibagué, Armenia, Manizales, Cúcuta e Cali. Além dos mortos e feridos, foram registrados danos em milhares de moradias, dezenas de casas foram completamente destruídas e 61 edifícios desabaram.


O governo decretou estado de calamidade nacional. Com a declaração de calamidade, o governo pode emitir resoluções para agilizar o atendimento imediato às vítimas, incluindo a contratações emergenciais. A declaração de calamidade pode durar até 12 meses, com possibilidade de prorrogação.


Abelardo de la Espriella foi a Chocó, enquanto seus ministros foram para o Eixo Cafeeiro (no centro-oeste do país) e o Valle (no sudoeste).


No Comitê Nacional de Gestão de Desastres, o presidente determinou que seu gabinete fosse enviado às regiões afetadas para coordenar o atendimento. A resposta emergencial é liderada pelo vice-presidente José Manuel Restrepo, que atua com o chanceler Omar Bula na articulação da cooperação internacional.


Postagem do vice-presidente, José Manuel Restrepo, em Manizales, no centro-oeste da Colômbia.


EUA prometem ajuda


O governo de Donald Trump destinou 15,5 milhões de dólares para abrigos de emergência, alimentos, proteção e avaliação dos danos causados pelo terremoto. O

CAF

 [Banco de Desenvolvimento da América Latina e Caribe] destinou 500 mil de dólares, e outros países também ofereceram apoio.


O presidente De la Espriella chegou ontem à noite a Cali, onde foi decretado toque de recolher e alguns pontos da cidade foram ocupados por militares para evitar saques em larga escala. As autoridades também decretaram alerta vermelho em todos os hospitais, que estão sobrecarregados devido ao grande número de feridos.


Várias capitais do país montaram pontos de coleta e arrecadação de doações para as vítimas do terremoto. Os colombianos pedem água potável, cobertores, mantas, travesseiros, colchonetes, alimentos não perecíveis, materiais de primeiros socorros e produtos de higiene pessoal.


O que dizem os protagonistas?


Abelardo de la Espriella (presidente recém-empossado):

 o presidente viajou a Chocó para acompanhar pessoalmente a crise e coordenou o Posto de Comando Unificado. “Vou estar à frente da resposta nacional e estarei presente em todos os territórios. Todos os ministros, o vice-presidente e o Posto de Comando Unificado se reportam a mim”, afirmou, após determinar que as operações de resgate dos sobreviventes fossem prioridade. “Sem diferenças ideológicas, devemos nos unir por esta causa” …

author: anred
title: Tras el retroceso del Gobierno, convocan a organizar una nueva marcha contra la ley de Milei
content:
Fotos: Andrés Manrique (ANRed).


Tras la masiva movilización del 6 de agosto que, junto con la falta de votos necesarios en el Senado, obligó al gobierno de Javier Milei a retroceder sobre el capítulo de extranjerización de tierras y la modificación de la Ley de Manejo del Fuego, empiezan a surgir las primeras convocatorias para discutir cómo continúa la lucha para cuando la Cámara de Diputados trate el proyecto de Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada. Por un lado, con la consigna «Los inmuebles públicos para las necesidades del pueblo», la Coordinadora Contra los Desalojos y por la Vivienda Digna y el Hábitat convoca a vecinas/os, casas colectivas, cooperativas, personas en situación de calle y a la comunidad a concentrarse este miércoles 12 de agosto a las 17 horas en Parque Lezama, en Defensa y Martín García (CABA). En tanto, Myriam Bregman, diputada del PTS-FIT, convoca

este jueves 13 de agosto a las 18 a una reunión en la Facultad de Ciencias Sociales de la UBA, donde se buscará comenzar a organizar una «Gran marcha de la bronca» que reúna las distintas demandas contra el Gobierno.

Por ANRed.


Luego de la masiva movilización del 6 de agosto contra la

Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada

que, junto con la falta de votos necesarios en el Senado,

obligó al gobierno de Javier Milei a retroceder sobre el capítulo de extranjerización de tierras y la modificación de la Ley de Manejo del Fuego

, desde diversos sectores empiezan a difundir las primeras convocatorias para discutir

cómo continúa la lucha para cuando la Cámara de Diputados trate el proyecto


que tuvo media sanción en el Senado

.


El Senado dio media sanción a la ley de Milei, pero la movilización anticipa una nueva batalla en Diputados


Por un lado, la

Coordinadora contra los Desalojos y por la Vivienda Digna y el Hábitat

 convoca a «vecinas, vecinos, casas colectivas, cooperativas, personas en situación de calle y a la comunidad» a concentrarse este

miércoles 12 de agosto a las 17 horas en Parque Lezama

, en Defensa y Martín García (CABA). La convocatoria se realiza luego de la aprobación en el Senado de los artículos vinculados a los

desalojos exprés y los límites a las expropiaciones

 incluidos en la ley. 

«

Ante la crisis y tras la aprobación en Senadores del capítulo de desalojos exprés y límites a las expropiaciones en la ‘ley de inviolabilidad de la propiedad privada’, nos organizamos para frenarlo en Diputados»

, señala la convocatoria.

Una publicación compartida por Consejerías de vivienda (@consejerias_de_vivienda)

Jorge Macri y a la Subsecretaría de Administración de Bienes Inmuebles

Guillermo Sánchez Sterli

Según los datos difundidos por la Coordinadora, durante el último año la gestión porteña habría subastado

más de 320 inmuebles y terrenos

. Además, entre abril de 2024 y marzo de 2026 se registraron más de 20 desalojos en inmuebles del GCBA, mientras que

permanecen activos más de 250 juicios de desalojo

 sobre propiedades de dominio de la Ciudad. La convocatoria también señala el ingreso de

$333.628.379 por remates sin destino justificado

.


Qué cambia para quienes alquilan con la nueva ley: «si no hay contrato ni recibos, hay desalojo en 72 horas»


“

Mientras hacen esto a la par de la Expo Real Estate, para servirle tierra pública a desarrolladores inmobiliarios, decimos BASTA

”, expresan las organizaciones, que reclaman el cese inmediato de los desalojos en inmuebles estatales y una mesa de trabajo urgente con la Subsecretaría de Bienes Inmuebles.


Entre sus demandas también incluyen la

aprobación de proyectos para modificar las leyes N° 52 y N° 6247

, el

traspaso de bienes al IVC para generar soluciones habitacionales

 o garantizar la prioridad de compra a sus habitantes, y el

cumplimiento del artículo 31 de la Constitución porteña junto con el rechazo al vaciamiento del Programa de Autogestión del Hábitat establecido por la Ley 341

.

author: A.N.A.
title: [Alemanha] Reflexões sobre a Solidariedade #1
content:
Thomas Meyer-Falk compartilhou conosco suas reflexões sobre a solidariedade e o sistema prisional:

 

Os muros (das prisões) não protegem as pessoas: protegem o status quo!

 

Passei quase 27 anos da minha vida na prisão. Onze desses anos foram em confinamento solitário. Já estou vivendo novamente em liberdade há três anos. Foi assim que compreendi que as prisões não são apenas edifícios de concreto e aço. Elas são também, sempre, uma expressão de uma sociedade que se apoia na exclusão; são, sobretudo, os membros marginalizados da sociedade que acabam na prisão.

 

Na escola, na grande mídia e até mesmo na mesa do bar (que hoje são as redes sociais), diz-se que as prisões servem à segurança. Na realidade, porém, elas administram o fracasso desta sociedade. Administram e punem a pobreza.

 

Vivenciei isso diretamente durante meus anos de prisão: quase todas as pessoas que encontrei viviam em condições precárias, e muitas tinham origem imigrante. Esse é o segundo fator central que coloca as pessoas na mira do sistema de justiça.

 

Vejo isso também na minha vida cotidiana desde que fui libertado, porque repetidas vezes me encontro sentado em audiências judiciais apenas para depois escrever sobre elas: quase sempre, as pessoas acusadas e condenadas são aquelas obrigadas a viver na pobreza. Em muitos casos, têm origem migrante.

 

Uma sociedade que gasta bilhões com militares, polícia, prisões e deportações, mas reduz investimentos em educação, saúde e inclusão social, cria precisamente as condições que depois pune por meio do direito penal.

 

São os prisioneiros anarquistas que nos lembram que a repressão é sempre também política. Aqueles que desafiam fundamentalmente a autoridade sentem o poder do Estado de maneira particularmente intensa.

 

Isso torna a solidariedade prática ainda mais importante: cartões-postais e cartas são um primeiro passo. Eles permitem que as pessoas presas saibam que alguém pensa nelas, que não foram esquecidas. Para mim, as muitas cartas que recebi, assim como a troca de ideias por correspondência — embora rigidamente monitorada pela prisão — ajudaram-me a sobreviver. Em alguns casos, dessa troca nasceram amizades que ainda perduram hoje.

 

A 

Semana Internacional de Solidariedade

 nos lembra que, juntos, defendemos a liberdade para e com as pessoas atrás das grades. É a nossa solidariedade que rompe o isolamento.

 

Por isso, a 

Semana Internacional de Solidariedade com os Prisioneiros Anarquistas

 é muito mais do que um gesto dirigido a indivíduos. É um lembrete de que a liberdade é indivisível. De que os muros não cercam apenas as prisões. Depois de quase três décadas preso, experimentei o quanto os muros externos penetraram profundamente em mim, mental e fisicamente. Libertar-se disso depois é um processo longo, mas tem mais chances de dar certo em um ambiente de solidariedade do que no frio da solidão.

 

Os muros não desaparecerão amanhã nem depois de amanhã; a 

Semana Internacional de Solidariedade

 provavelmente continuará existindo por muitos anos.

 

Para algumas pessoas, o impacto de uma semana de solidariedade pode parecer pequeno. Mas, sem essa pequena contribuição, tudo permanecerá como está.

author: Darío Aranda
title: Ley de tierras: "Pretenden despojar a las comunidades indígenas de sus territorios"
content:
OPINIÓN


Por Silvina Ramírez*


La Cámara de Senadores dio media sanción a la llamada "Ley de inviolabilidad de la propiedad privada", a pesar de un rechazo generalizado que obligó al oficialismo a resignar el capítulo sobre extranjerización de la tierra y las modificaciones a la Ley de Manejo del Fuego. Sin embargo, siguió adelante con dos temas centrales: modificaciones al régimen de expropiaciones y de desalojos. En el primer caso, requiere de más condiciones para declarar la utilidad pública de un bien inmueble para luego expropiar; en el segundo, flexibiliza el procedimiento, lo agiliza para facilitar los desalojos.


Es probable que la discusión en Diputados llegue con otras sorpresas y otras negociaciones. De la lectura de lo aprobado, y específicamente alrededor de los desalojos, pueden extraerse las siguientes

consecuencias e impactos para las comunidades indígenas

, siempre amenazadas, que hoy carecen de lo que es tan valiosa y ponderada para el sector empresarial, pero totalmente ignorada para el mundo indígena: la seguridad jurídica.


En primer lugar, la acción de desalojo para inmuebles urbanos y rurales se sustanciará por el procedimiento establecido para juicios sumarísimos. En otras palabras, y evitando tecnicismos,

los plazos se acortan, no se admiten excepciones previas, los abogados no puede presentar alegatos

 y las apelaciones —revisión de la medida— son restrictivas.


Con esta modificación normativa, con la instalación del “desalojo exprés”, las amenazas a las comunidades indígenas se profundizan. De hecho, es una herramienta creada a medida para aquellos que pretenden despojar a las comunidades indígenas de sus territorios. Todo legalmente y a través de la vía judicial, cercenando la posibilidad del debate judicial.


En segundo lugar, amplía la legitimación activa o permite que cualquier persona que invoque un derecho o interés legítimo puede presentar la acción de desalojo. En territorios en donde los títulos siempre son oscuros, en donde la manipulación, la corrupción, y el favorecimiento para unos pocos están a la orden del día, la posibilidad de que, prácticamente, cualquier individuo pueda iniciar una causa judicial, complejiza mucho más el escenario.


Las comunidades indígenas están habituadas al hostigamiento judicial. Esta ley que hoy tiene media sanción

facilita la persecución judicial a través del litigio, restándole mecanismos de defensa a quienes defienden sus territorios

, invocando los derechos territoriales reconocidos por la legislación vigente.


Foto: Alex Dukal / LUAN - Colectiva fotográfica


Una ley de tierras para un modelo que arrasa territorios


Lo que el Senado logró aprobar en

una sesión atravesada por protestas

 en todo el país

 no es una medida aislada. Aunque debió ceder frente a su pretensión de liberar la extranjerización de la tierra, y modificar el destino y los plazos de las tierras incendiadas, insistió en votar el proyecto de ley para modificar la expropiación y el desalojo.


Esto debe, necesariamente, vincularse con el conjunto de acciones que viene llevando delante de forma consistente —vale sólo pensar en el

R

egimen de Incentivo para Grandes Interviones (RIGI

) y en el

Súper RIGI

—, y que responde a un modelo económico, una matriz productiva y energética, un modelo de desarrollo, que demanda para su consolidación de territorios despejados, territorios vacíos.


Las comunidades indígenas son uno de los principales sujetos afectados. No sólo por el desconocimiento de sus derechos, sino porque prolijamente se fue desarticulando un andamiaje que, aunque precario, permitía austeramente avanzar hacia la titulación colectiva. La

derogación de la

Ley de Emergencia de la Posesión y Propiedad Comunitaria Indígena (26.160)

, es sólo una señal de los objetivos perseguidos por la actual gestión de gobierno.


No obstante, se debe insistir en el estatus que revisten las carpetas técnicas, producto del relevamiento técnico jurídico catastral que ordenó la derogada ley. Éstas son expresión de un acto administrativo del Estado con efecto jurídico. La ley invistió como autoridad de aplicación al INAI. Más allá del cambio de este instituto en el organigrama del Estado, independiente de la derogación de la ley, las carpetas técnicas fueron resultado de un trabajo con las comunidades indígenas y no pueden soslayarse, aunque parece ser la intención de la gestión de gobierno cuando va anulando, de a poco, carpetas que son problemáticas para otros …

author: Isabel Ortega
title: Comunidades originarias celebran séptima Asamblea Nacional por el Agua
content:
En días pasados, 8 y 9 de agosto, fue celebrada la séptima Asamblea Nacional por el Agua, la Vida y el Territorio, convocatoria que desde 2022 reune a colectividades y comunidades originarias de todo México que luchan contra proyectos y empresas que amenazan las fuentes de agua en sus territorios.

La asamblea tuvo lugar en Zitacua, Nayarit, territorio donde se defiende el río San Pedro Mezquital, amenazado por el proyecto estatal de la presa “El Nayar”. A la convocatoria respondieron poco menos de quinientas personas, entre ellas integrantes de 18 pueblos originarios, así como participantes de 18 estados de México y seis países más.

Las colectividades y comunidades asistentes defienden, en sus respectivos territorios, ríos, cuencas, manantiales, acuíferos, lagos, lagunas, humedales, playas, bahías y cerros, enfrentando amenazas relacionadas a proyectos estatales, privados y extractivos, tales como el fracking, presas hidroeléctricas, basureros y rellenos sanitarios, la industria farmacéutica, el agronegocio, así como procesos como la urbanización, y actividades ilícitas como la deforestación por tala ilegal.

En la declaratoria emitida por esta Séptima Asamblea, las comunidades reunidas resaltaron algunos proyectos que amenazan a los cuerpos de agua en sus territorios, entre estos, como el Plan Hídrico del Noroeste, proyecto de infraestructura hidráulica que busca redistribuir una enorme cantidad de agua, principalmente del Río Santiago, en el norte de Nayarit, hacia Sinaloa y Sonora, a través de la construcción de túneles. La asamblea también denunció las amenazas que enfrenta la cuenca Chapala-Santiago, donde los ríos Santiago y Ameca podrían ser devastados por la actividad industrial.

En este contexto de amenazas a los ríos y fuentes de agua de sus comunidades, quienes integran la Asamblea llamaron a seguir fortaleciendo la lucha por la vida en los territorios: “Defender el agua es defender la vida, defender el territorio es defender nuestra historia, defender la autonomía es defender el futuro de nuestros hijos. Los pueblos originarios no luchamos solo por nuestras comunidades, luchamos por el equilibrio de la naturaleza, la biodiversidad, los bosques, ríos, y el derecho de la futuras generaciones de vivir en un planeta donde aún exista vida”, afirmaron en la declaratoria final del encuentro.

Por otra parte, las comunidades reunidas en la Asamblea Nacional por el Agua, la Vida y el Territorio, se posicionaron frente a la próxima consulta relativa a la iniciativa de reforma de la Ley de pueblos indígenas y afrodescendientes, impulsada por el gobierno federal, herramienta legislativa que consideran que busca facilitar el despojo del territorio de los pueblos originarios.

En la declaratoria del evento, las comunidades firmantes exigieron que el Río San Pedro Mezquital sea declarado sujeto de derecho, así como la cancelación total del proyecto El Nayar, antes conocido como “Las Fuentes” que se pretende imponer sobre este río. En este mismo sentido, la Asamblea también exigió respeto a los cuerpos de agua que forman parte de sitios sagrado de peregrinación y ceremonia de los pueblos Naayeri, O’dam, Wixarika y Meshican que habitan esta región.

Por último, las comunidades reunidas en la séptima Asamblea Nacional por el Agua, la Vida y el Territorio llamaron a una serie de acciones en los próximos meses, entre ellas, convocaron a acompañar las movilizaciones convocadas por familias buscadoras en todo el país en el marco del día internacional de la desaparición forzada, que será el próximo 30 de agosto. De igual manera, llamaron a quienes integran la Asamblea a sumarse al evento conmemorativo por los 30 años de la fundación del Congreso Nacional Indígena, a celebrarse del 10 al 12 de octubre en la Casa de los Pueblos “Samir Flores Soberanes” en la Ciudad de México.

author: CMI Argentina
title: ATE logró la reincorporación de trabajadoras y trabajadores despedidos en PAMI
content:
“Desde la primera cesantía decidimos que íbamos a confrontarlos en todos los planos. No sólo dimos la batalla judicial, se multiplicaron los paros y fueron numerosas las protestas en la sede central de la obra social”, aseguró Rodolfo Aguiar.


La Asociación Trabajadores del Estado (ATE) logró la reincorporación de trabajadoras y trabajadores de PAMI que habían sido despedidos sin causa por la gestión de Javier Milei durante el mes de abril. “Hoy debemos celebrar una nueva demostración de que luchar siempre sirve”, destacó Rodolfo Aguiar, Secretario General del sindicato.


“Desde la primera cesantía decidimos que íbamos a confrontarlos en todos los planos. No sólo dimos la batalla judicial, se multiplicaron los paros y fueron numerosas las protestas en la sede central de la obra social”, detalló el dirigente nacional.


En esta línea, Aguiar resaltó: “Siento un orgullo inmenso por esta ATE que no se resigna y que lucha incansablemente contra las injusticias provocadas por un Gobierno que quiere aniquilar todos derechos. No lo van a lograr”.


Cabe destacar que entre las y los trabajadores despedidos de la obra social de jubilados se encontraban representantes gremiales como es el caso de Melina Gutiérrez, Secretaria General de la Junta Interna del organismo en Rosario. De esta forma, las cesantías incurrieron en una clara violación a la Ley de Asociaciones Sindicales Nº 23.551 que establece la tutela sindical.


Además de librar la batalla judicial, desde la organización gremial se manifestaron “desde el primer día” en el sector de trabajo de los cesanteados como así también realizaron numerosas protestas en la sede central de PAMI, informaron desde ATE.


Por esta apuesta a mantener alta la conflictividad es que, consideraron desde el sindicato, se logró la medida tomada por el Juzgado Nacional de 1ra Instancia del Trabajo nro. 77, el cual dio lugar al reclamo de ATE obligando al Gobierno a reinstalar en sus puestos de trabajo a los despedidos.

author: Bruna Bronoski
title: Banco do Nordeste e Itaú financiam R$ 44 milhões para soja em área de conflito no Maranhão
content:
“Eles entravam de madrugada [os tratores]. Quando você via, o estrago estava feito. Quando a gente chegava lá, paravam. Chamávamos a polícia e, quando eles vinham [os policiais], ainda ficavam a favor deles [dos tratoristas], que tinham o documento”, conta Edvaldo Dutra, morador do assentamento Veredão, ao lembrar dos episódios de derrubada das florestas de bacuri na área rural de Chapadinha, extremo leste do Maranhão.


Antes dos primeiros episódios de “correntão” — quando uma enorme corrente de aço ligada a dois tratores de esteira destrói toda a fauna e flora que vê pela frente —, os moradores do Veredão e do assentamento vizinho, a Vila dos Borges/Sangue, acampavam temporariamente nas áreas mais altas para caçar bacuri. O fruto do Cerrado enche os bacurizais de dezembro a março.


Desde 2022, no entanto, homens, mulheres e crianças deixam tudo para trás ao primeiro som da zoada de tratores, em qualquer período do ano, e sobem às pressas para a chapada. 


O sojicultor paulista responsável pelas derrubadas é Gustavo Maretto de Barros. A GMB Investimentos Holding, que leva suas iniciais, foi aberta em 2020. Pouco tempo depois, a empresa adquiriu terras entre os dois assentamentos, interrompendo um processo de conversão de possíveis terras devolutas do Maranhão em assentamentos, hoje tradicionalmente ocupadas pelas famílias. 


Ministério Público do Maranhão denunciou à Justiça uso de correntão pela GMB entre as comunidades Veredão e Vila dos Borges em 29 de fevereiro de 2024 (Fonte: imagens cedidas)


Barros é sócio-administrador de ao menos 11 empresas ativas, cujo capital social somado chega aos R$ 58,8 milhões. Espalhados nos estados de Tocantins, Pará, Goiás e São Paulo, os negócios vão de aluguel de máquinas e equipamentos agrícolas, cultivo e comércio de café e gado, à compra, venda e incorporação de imóveis. 


Em Chapadinha, o empresário tem conseguido autorizações ambientais, registros cartoriais e financiamento para levar a cabo o seu plano: substituir milhares de hectares de florestas nativas do Cerrado por plantios de soja na região do extremo leste maranhense. Mais do que isso, tem obtido financiamento com recursos subsidiados e linhas de apoio supostamente voltadas à sustentabilidade. 


“Ele veio e destruiu tudo”, conta seu Anastácio*, extrativista de bacuri da Vila dos Borges. “A gente chorou. Preocupados porque era o alimento e a fonte de renda que a gente tinha.”


A reportagem entrou em contato com Gustavo Maretto de Barros, que

respondeu

 em nota que a reivindicação de uso tradicional dos extrativistas “não procede”. A justificativa dele é de que os camponeses não têm capacidade de exercer atividade econômica no local.


“Veredão e Sangue juntos possuem mais de 5.500 hectares, ainda assim, há interesse em mais área?”, questiona Barros. As cerca de 200 famílias das duas comunidades estão oficialmente sobre uma área de 5.856 hectares, ocupada coletivamente, que corresponderia a 29 hectares por unidade familiar. O sojicultor, sozinho, vinculou 5.363 hectares às operações de crédito rural com o Itaú e o Banco do Nordeste do Brasil.


Juros subsidiados para desmatar o Matopiba 


Desde o início do conflito fundiário com extrativistas de Veredão e Vila dos Borges, Gustavo Barros teria recebido R$ 44,3 milhões via política pública de

crédito rural

 para plantar soja em Chapadinha, apontam informações do

Instituto DADOS

, organização técnico-jurídica que fortalece a justiça socioambiental e climática no Brasil.


Ao todo, foram seis financiamentos firmados a partir de abril de 2022 por meio do Banco do Nordeste do Brasil (BNB) e do banco privado Itaú, com prazos para pagar até 2037. 


O ano da primeira operação de financiamento, 2022, coincide com o período em que os extrativistas relatam as primeiras perturbações no território. Na ocasião, o BNB depositou R$ 11,6 milhões na conta do empresário para a compra de máquinas, tratores, reboques, carretas e equipamentos de carga. 


Quando o financiamento foi concedido, em dezembro daquele ano, a área vinculada à operação já tinha perdido mil hectares de vegetação nativa, revela o cruzamento de dados feito pelo

Joio

 com informações do crédito rural na plataforma

Global Forest Watch

(GFW). Nos anos seguintes, o desmatamento continuou.


A fonte de recursos de todas as operações do BNB para a área de Gustavo Barros é o Fundo Constitucional de Financiamento do Nordeste (FNE), um recurso controlado pelo sistema de crédito rural. Desde janeiro deste …

author: La Zarzamora
title: En la defensa de la tierra, arde tu memoria!!! Brujo presente
content:
El pasado Lunes 3 de agosto a las 6:40 de la mañana decidimos cortar el tren que comunica la Capital (Ciudad de Buenos Aires) y la ciudad de La Plata en el territorio dominado por el estado sionista de Argentina.

Esta acción se da en el marco de la reivindicación de la memoria del compañero anarquista Santiago Maldonado, el Lechu, a 9 años de su asesinato a manos de la Gendarmería Nacional en la comunidad mapuche Cushamen. Cada vez que comienza el mes de agosto, es un llamado tanto a reflexionar como a actuar, no solo desde el recuerdo, sino desde la lucha anárquica, la solidaridad y el apoyo mutuo.

Cada agosto intentamos recordarlo mediante la acción, no desde el martirologio, sino porque Santiago era uno de nosotrxs y como su asesinato repercutió en el entorno anarquista. Odiando el manoseo que ya hecho tanto el estado como la prensa y la izquierda, con su identidad y porque cada día que pasa en esta sociedad siniestra y tecnologizada su práctica nos recuerda lo que importa: la defensa de la naturaleza y la lucha por la liberación total.

En ese sentido decidimos cortar la vía a la altura del arroyo El Gato, donde se pretende construir la nueva bajada de la Autopista a City Bell, devastando humedales a su paso en pos de la circulación de personas como de mercaderías, profundizando la destrucción de lo poco que queda de la vida silvestre en las grandes ciudades.

¡Fuego a la sociedad industrial y a sus defensores!

¡Libertad a Milton y Eneas y a todxs lxs presxs!

author: groundxero
title: Who were the Luddites? Their legacy ripples through politics, cultural commentary and literature
content:
But who exactly were the Luddites? They were a collective reaction to the traumas

of the Industrial Revolution, in early industrial England

.


 


by

Brian Lewis

,

McGill University


 


American filmmaker

George Lucas

 is one of the latest to indicate he’s open to AI in the movie industry. In a recent interview,

the director said

 resistance to the technology was “very much like sitting here saying: ‘Well, I believe the horse and the buggy is really where it’s at. These cars, they break down, they need gas, there’s all kinds of problems with them and pretty soon they’ll be making them into tanks, and then they’ll be killing people. It’s terrible.’”


 


The Guardian

 story was headlined:

“George Lucas likens AI sceptics to luddites clinging to horses and carts.”


 


“Luddites” have sometimes stood in for enemies of progress: those destined to be swept aside in the forward march of history.


 


The label

of “neo-Luddism”

 or “digital Luddite” is also being reclaimed by people concerned about labour conditions, society and democracy in an era of AI expansion

twinned with personal profit

.


 


But who exactly were the Luddites? They were a collective reaction to the traumas

of the Industrial Revolution, in early industrial England

.


 


Their legacy has been profound, as suggested by both negative and positive polemics related to them in intellectual and cultural commentary, art and literature and

popular histories produced

 as

digital technology continues

 to grow.


 


When trade unions were illegal


 


As the new political economy, fuelled by transatlantic slavery and colonial extraction, began to transform work practices in England and introduce new forms of mechanization,

skilled artisans and weavers resisted

. They sought to protect their livelihoods, their ways of life and their communities.


 


Trade unions were illegal and the workers did not have political representation. Co-operative societies did not yet exist and state welfare was a distant dream. The only alternative to acquiescence was what historian

Eric Hobsbawm

 memorably called “collective bargaining by riot.”


 


Food riots, destroying machinery or setting fire to factories

 were in-your-face ways to get employers and local authorities to pay attention to their legitimate grievances.


 


When the English cartoonist Charles Williams depicted a veterinarian and a blacksmith violently attacking dandies on bicycles for undermining traditional horse-drawn transportation in 1819, the blacksmith’s smashing with a mallet was a clear reference to the spasm of machine-wrecking earlier in the decade.


 


Williams’s caricature came within a few years of the mass outbreak in Britain when the terms Luddism and Luddite became commonplace.


Cartoon by Charles Williams showing a veterinary surgeon and a blacksmith attacking dandies on bicycles representing the anti-bicycle movement. (Wikimedia), CC BY


Famous episodes of Luddism


 


Historians agree that the most

f

amous episode of Luddism began in 1811

 in Nottinghamshire in the English Midlands.


 


A group of stocking weavers formed a secret organization, purportedly led by a certain Ned Ludd, a fictitious

figure also styled as Captain, General or King Ludd

.


‘Leader of the Luddites’ hand-coloured etching from 1812. (British Museum)


In the context of widespread economic misery caused by

the war against Napoleon

, the weavers blamed new, wide-frame knitting machines for stealing their jobs, reducing their earnings and making a bad situation worse. In targeted attacks, they smashed more than 1,000 of the stocking frames, and the property destruction then spread to the textile weaving and spinning districts of Lancashire and Yorkshire.


 


Fearing the revolutionary potential of this wave of violence — and that

English plebeians might follow the French example and overthrow

 the old regime — the government cracked down hard. It sent in 12,000 troops to quell the riots, and

members of Parliament voted overwhelmingly to make

 frame-breaking a hanging offence.


 


The ruling classes managed to restore order, despite sporadic outbreaks until 1816, punctuating their clampdown with exemplary hangings and

sentences of transportation to Australia

. Their determination to prevent revolution, protect property and enable unfettered economic expansion was patently clear.

author: rti_admin
title: A Decade Later…
content:
I have been meaning to write about this journey for a long time. I always imagined it would be an essay. But when I signed up for the Bosla Arts and Studio 12 Open Mic Solidarity Night in London in June 2026, poetry felt like the only honest form.

The spirit of that evening – the refusal of silence, the insistence on being heard – reminded me of something I had recited every morning as a child in a hostel in Telangana: I am not inferior to anyone—one of the ten commandments of SWAEROES.

So I went. And I performed this poem. I wrote about an earlier part of this journey in a 2023 essay for the Round Table India. This poem begins where that essay ends.

A Chair I Never Dreamed I’d Sit On

This photograph was taken when I was 17 years old, after my live-telecast television class that was broadcast on MANA TV to students across 268 Social Welfare Residential Schools in Telangana.

The lesson was part of the S. R. Shankaran Super Students programme, one of the many visionary initiatives introduced by Dr R. S. Praveen Kumar. Built around the motto Earn While You Learn, the programme encouraged students to develop their teaching and public speaking skills by delivering live television lessons to fellow students. Those selected to teach also received an honorarium in recognition of their work.

After each live session, the student-teacher would visit Dr. Praveen Kumar’s office, where he would personally congratulate them and present the cash award. In this photograph, he invited me to sit in his chair – a gesture of encouragement and belief that meant far more to me than I could fully understand at the time.

The cash award rests on the desk in front of us. Behind us hangs a portrait of Dr B. R. Ambedkar. It is a photograph I have always held especially close to my heart. Like so many memories from my years in the Social Welfare Residential Schools, this photograph reminds me of the opportunities we were given to dream beyond our circumstances.

Back then, we did not have smartphones or easy ways to take and preserve photographs. Years later, someone who had kept this picture found a way to reach me through mutual friends and shared it with me. I am deeply grateful they did, because they preserved more than a photograph. They preserved a moment that represents not just an achievement, but an entire chapter of my life – one that continues to shape and inspire me today.

Born the youngest of three daughters

in a small town in rural Telangana,

I was the one who always wanted to study, study, study,

Before the question had even found its end.

There was a small school in the village.

We went when we were little, my sisters and I.

But fees have a way of growing.

My father heard about the social welfare schools.

Free. Residential. For children like us.

toward making it all mean something,

through everything difficult and dark,

with a love that asked nothing in return.

I shall be a leader wherever I am.

I shall always think big and aim high.

When Dr. R.S. Praveen Kumar sir

Elocution. Debate competitions.

Super Students, earn while you learn.

Coaching for law, coaching for accountancy,

whatever door you wanted to walk through,

Between the ages of ten and seventeen,

Confidence built in small rooms

where nobody had expected to find it.

I shall always think big and aim high.

At 17, when we were leaving those schools,

We had roads leading in every direction.

Law. Accountancy. Sciences. Arts.

Whichever door we wanted to open,

There was coaching, preparation, and a way in.

You do not make it wait or come back later.

You figure out the rest on the other side.

Economics. Another state. A new city.

For someone who had never left home,

Bangalore felt like the whole world.

This is the furthest I will go.

I shall always think big and aim high.

At 18, in that same university,

in a way no classroom ever had.

In our social welfare schools, we were all the same.

all from families the system had pushed to the edge,

Caste was not the wall between us.

But here the air was different.

In the way people looked at you,

Dr B. R. Ambedkar had already named it.

My whole community had endured it.

That same university also gave me the tools.

to think about it, to sit with it,

to understand it not just as pain

something that had been unfolding

To change the direction of everything.

They are still there, guiding every path.

I applied for everything again.

as long as I was not doing nothing.

And then I heard …

author: Angelina Guo
title: 「寫作是最後一道防線」：巴勒斯坦詩人亞赫亞·哈馬納專訪
content:
哈馬納（Yahya Al Hamarna）是來自加薩走廊的巴勒斯坦作家、學者和難民。他曾在加薩的愛資哈爾（Al-Azhar）大學研修政治學、國際關係與外交。他的寫作聚焦於人權、正義、國際法與全球政治，而他的詩歌則探索戰爭下的記憶、流放、愛與生存。他的作品透過保留意圖被暴力所抹殺的那些聲音、場景和日常點滴而深深錕刻在巴勒斯坦的當代記憶中。他的首部充滿辛酸的詩集《我的聲音無法被炸毀》（My Voice Cannot Be Bombed）於2025年由伊斯克拉書局（Iskra Books）發表。他的許多摘錄透過社群媒體流向世界。由卡亞爾（Elissa Kayal），薩圖夫（Nada Sattouf）與杜福爾（Alycia Dufour）共同翻譯的《我的聲音無法被炸毀》法語版本最近由魁北克的多林出版社（Éditions de la Rue Dorion）與法國的八月伯恩出版社（Burn∼Août）出版。

我第一次看到哈馬納的作品是在社群媒體Instagram上，當時我的大學同學，一位優秀的詩人愛麗莎（Elissa）分享了《我的聲音無法被炸毀》的節錄。當我在台北的公寓裡讀到這本書時，我被他的文字所展現出的優雅與堅忍所深深震撼。幾個月之後，我們開始彼此交流。儘管面臨網路斷聯，充電困難，寫作媒介缺乏等諸多不便，哈馬納還是熱情接受了為台灣《破土》雜誌所做的書面採訪。在被佔領土加薩持續遭受種族滅絕，醫院學校被炸，房屋家庭被毀的當下，《我的聲音無法被炸毀》如同一份見證，不僅展示了文字的力量，巴勒斯坦人的尊嚴與抵抗，也寄託了哈馬納希望重返學業，重回自由祖國的夢想。

郭佳：你能否介紹一下《我的聲音無法被炸毀》寫作過程的更多細節？這本書的寫作時期2023年至2025年正是巴勒斯坦被持續佔領和破壞，物質條件極度惡化的時期。在開頭一首詩歌中，你寫道：「寫作遠非紙上論道，它是生存方式，它是抵抗之聲，它是明日諾言。」你是如何開始詩歌寫作的，你又如何描述你與文學的關係？

哈馬納：我並不是為了要當一位詩人而開始寫作。我開始寫作是因為我需要一個安置內心的地方。我的童年在加薩度過，我對那裡的歷史、故事與書中描繪的生活很著迷。在聯合國近東救濟工程處（UNRWA）開辦的難民學校裡，我發現文字可以保留會被暴力與時間抹去的東西。我開始記錄感想，創作短詩，以此嘗試了解周遭的世界，為難以言說的情感尋求解答。我的家人，尤其是我的母親，一直鼓勵我繼續寫作，文學慢慢成為我生命的一部分。我出生於2001年8月11日。隨著年紀增長，我變成一個安靜的小孩，喜歡用文字表達自己的想法。然後在2008年12月，我經歷了人生的第一次戰爭和第一次流離失所。 2009年1月，同樣的經驗再一次上演。我是難民，但是我渴望向世界證明我們理當擁有生存的權利。我在學業上成績優秀，在歷史方面特別突出。我學習了很多歷史知識，也閱讀過涵蓋殖民主義、革命、印度、美洲和蘇聯等很多書。後來我決定選修政治學並在許多民間團體當志工。我夢想旅遊，因為我從未有過外出遠行的經歷，我還夢想現場觀看皇家馬德里的足球比賽。我想擁有自己的家庭，享受被世界溫柔相待的感覺。只要我的旅行在繼續，我的生命在繼續，我的故事就會繼續下去。

當2023年的種族屠殺開始之後，我的寫作性質發生了徹底改變。寫作不再只是一種藝術實踐，而是變成了一種心理與情感上的生存手段。我在難民營的帳篷裡、在被摧毀的建築廢墟旁、在被迫疏散的路途上、在電力、網路甚至寧靜都統統消失的生活中進行寫作。我在燭光下記錄，在僅存不多電量的手機上打字，在零碎的紙片上書寫，只因為害怕丟失一切。

《我的聲音無法被炸毀》這本書的成型並無事先規劃，它只是詩作日積月累的自然結果。我的每一篇文字都在試圖挽救尚未消失的生活片段。我想要留住那些會被戰爭抹去的平凡瞬間：麵包的香氣、母親的聲音、祖父母在扎爾諾卡（Zarnoqa）村里種下的橘子樹、伴隨著咖啡與費魯茲（Fairuz）音樂的早晨、與朋友的交談、大學夢想，以及對平凡未來的靜靜盼望。我意識到記憶本身已經成為一種抵抗運動。

就我而言，文學從來不是一條逃避現實的路徑，而是一種更深層切入現實的方法。詩歌讓我得以訴說悲傷但不就此屈服，談論希望但不否認苦難。詩歌能夠提醒我，即便家園盡毀，語言仍能建構一方天地，讓人性得以存續。

我常說，寫作是最後的防線。在建築被傾毀之前，他們試圖抹去我們的故事；而在抹去故事之前，他們又試圖讓我們保持沉默。我寫下的每一首詩，都是我對被消失命運的抗爭。這是我向世界宣告的方式，即我們不只是新聞標題或統計數據——我們是有血有肉的人類，有愛和夢想，有求知慾望，有歡笑和記憶，還有對未來的不斷憧憬。

郭佳：在《我的聲音無法被炸毀》一書中，你講述了自己與祖父穆斯塔法（Mustafa）一同前往加沙的經歷，途中你因攜帶一支鋼筆而被哨兵逮捕，原因是他認定鋼筆是一件危險武器。能否請你多談談你的祖父，以及你與故土之間的情感連結？

哈馬納：我的祖父穆斯塔法教我懂得，你只有把家鄉裝在心裡才能在將來的某一天回到那裡。我的祖父出生在扎爾諾卡（Zarnoqa）,一個以橘子園和富饒的土地而聞名的地方。 1948年大逃亡時，他同幾十萬巴勒斯坦人被迫時離家鄉。他到加薩時只有很少的隨身物品，但卻有完整的，永遠不會消失的家鄉記憶。

在我成長的過程中，每當我的祖父談起札爾諾卡，我總是聚精會神地聆聽。他描述家鄉時放佛不是在談論一個已經湮沒於歷史長河中的地方，而是當天清晨他在那裡的街道漫步的地方。他記得那裡的橙花、無花果樹與橄欖樹、水井、田野，還有在那裡生活的村民。這些故事成了我最初的地理啟蒙課。在從課本中知曉各國名稱之前，我已先透過祖父的記憶，在腦海中勾勒出了巴勒斯坦的版圖。

我的祖母薩菲亞（Safiyya）也活在這些記憶之中。我至今仍記得她烤製的麵包香氣、家庭聚會的溫馨，以及在一切被戰爭改變之前，那段平凡生活中的質樸美好。這些尋常細節看似微不足道，卻構成了我寫作的基石。它們時時刻刻提醒著我：巴勒斯坦不僅是土地，更是由家庭、歌謠、食譜、花園、歡笑與童年記憶交織而成的家。

在一首詩中，我想像自己因隨身攜帶一支鋼筆而遭到士兵攔截。這一具有像徵意義的場景反映了這樣的現實，那就是記憶本身已被視為一種危險。一支筆雖然無法摧毀建築，卻能守護那段他人試圖抹去的歷史。正因如此，寫作成了我回歸故土的方式，即便我無法在現實中踏上那片土地。

對我而言，故土遠不止於一個地理概念，它更關乎記憶、語言、人際連結與文化傳承。即便我輾轉流離失所，巴勒斯坦始終活在我的內心深處。只要我記得祖輩傳承給我的故事，並堅持將其書寫下來，我就深知，我的故土絕不會被抹去。

郭佳：能否談談您所掌握的語言以及您與母語之間的關係？ 《我的聲音無法被炸毀》的法文版是從阿拉伯文翻譯直接翻譯而來，而您的首部詩集則是用英文出版的。您會用多種語言創作詩歌嗎？

哈馬納：阿拉伯語是我隨心而動的語言。它是母親說給我聽的第一語言，是祖父母用來講述巴勒斯坦故事的語言，也是我初次做夢時使用的語言。每次提筆寫作，我總會自然而然地回歸到阿拉伯語，因為從童年起它便用韻律、情感與文化記憶來塑造我。

儘管《我的聲音無法被炸毀》最初是以英語出版的，但其中的每一首詩其實都誕生於阿拉伯語。這部英文譯本的問世，離不開那些語言功底深厚，對詩歌內涵理解尊重的譯者們的精心翻譯與緊密合作。這次看到詩集作品直接從阿拉伯語譯成法語，對我來說又是一次令人感動的經驗。這讓我意識到，儘管語言各異，人類的情感仍能跨越語言的界限，產生共鳴。

我偶爾也會用英語寫作，特別是與世界各地的讀者交流或在社群媒體上分享簡短感悟的時候。但詩創作則別有不同。每當我寫詩時，我通常會先用阿拉伯語構思，因為意象往往會先在阿拉伯語中浮現。詞語的音韻、句子的節奏，甚至那份沉默本身，都首先屬於阿拉伯語，而後才屬於其他語言。

對我來說，翻譯不只是將一種語言的語句轉換成另一種語言，它更是一種基於信任的互動。好的譯者不僅傳達語句的意義，更會傳遞其內在的精髓。我很幸運能與那些優秀的譯者合作，他們在翻譯詩歌的同時，也將有關加薩、巴勒斯坦、記憶與希望的殘片嵌入新的語言之中。

每一次新的語言版本，都彷彿是在一間許多人認為已埋於廢墟之下的房屋裡開啟了一扇新窗。這讓我明白，文學不為疆域所限，即便作者無法遠行，詩歌仍能繼續它的旅程。

郭佳：看到自己的作品廣為流傳，有何感受？能否分享一下在詩歌網絡傳播過程中，那些令你難忘或有意義的經驗？

哈馬納：我生命中最大的悖論之一，便是我雖然無法離開加沙，但我的文字卻已遠播至這片土地之外。

讓我至為感動的是，我在沒有水電的難民帳篷裡，在無人機的噪音中寫下的詩歌，竟然能夠跨越山水，走進蒙特利爾、溫哥華、多倫多、得克薩斯、加利福尼亞、亞利桑那、巴塞羅那、巴黎、馬賽、斯旺西、卡迪夫、滕比、都靈、那不勒斯、托斯卡納、蘇黎世、布魯塞爾、奧列巴、英國無數個其他人無法列舉的中。每一篇譯文、每一次朗讀、每一個訊息都在提醒我：文學能夠建構獨有的，不受檢查站或國界限制的地理版圖。

對我而言，社群媒體早已超越了單純平台的意義。它變成一座橋樑，讓我藉此認識來自世界各地的譯者、作家、藝術家、學生、音樂人和讀者。他們將我的詩作譯成我從未想過會觸及的語言。他們將我的文字融入畫作，在文學節上朗誦，在書展上推廣。他們還直接給我寫信，分享我的詩句如何在他們的心中久久迴盪。

讓我深受觸動的是，當我身陷加薩之時，素不相識的人們卻在世界各地組織閱讀活動，朗誦《我的聲音無法被炸毀》。他們將我的文字帶到了我無法親臨的地方，讓我明白，一旦文學作品公之於眾，它便不再屬於某一個人，而是融入到人類的共同敘事當中。

我所獲得的最大回報莫過於發現「同情」同樣能夠跨越山海。在難以想像的滿目瘡痍中，我收穫了遍布全球的友誼。許多人因著詩歌與我結識，也因著對人性尊嚴、正義與希望的共同信念而選擇駐留。

我收到的每一則留言，雖然語言各異，但都在傳遞著同樣的訊息，即沒有任何圍牆能夠高到足以阻擋同理心，也沒有任何炸彈的威力能夠蓋過真誠的聲音。

郭佳：您最喜歡的作家有哪些？對您影響最深的人或書籍又是哪些？您最近還在創作新的詩嗎？您最近一切都好嗎？

哈馬納：我覺得每位作家的心裡都藏著一座小小的圖書館，我也不例外。

在巴勒斯坦作家中，加桑·卡納法尼（Ghassan Kanafani）讓我明白，文學與正義密不可分。他的作品向我展示了即便身處流亡之中，文學故事依然能夠發揮對身分認同、尊嚴與集體記憶的守護作用。他的小說，尤其是《重返海法》（Returning to Haifa）、《陽光下的人們》（Men in the Sun）和《烏姆·薩阿德》（Umm Saad），至今仍是我理解文學與巴勒斯坦的重要讀物。馬哈茂德·達爾維什（Mahmoud …

title: Serok Barzanî pêşwaziyê li Parlamenterekî Almanyayê kir
content:
Roja Yekşemê 9ê Tebaxa 2026an li Pîrmamê Serok Mesûd Barzanî pêşwaziyê li birêz Serdar Yuksel endamê Parlementoya Almanyayê kir. Di hevdîtinê de Serok Barzanî bi germî bixêrhatina birêz Serdar Yuksel kir û kêfxweşiya xwe anî ziman ku ciwanekî Kurd kariye di navendên siyasî û parlementoyî yên Almanyayê de rolek hebe û destxweşî li hewl û keda wî ya di warên curbecur de û di parastina doza Kurd û penaberan li Almanyayê de kir. Her wiha digel balkişandina li ser bingeh û prensîbên xebata rizgarîxwaziya gelê Kurdistanê, tekez li ser aştîxwazbûna doza gelê Kurdistanê kir ku divê pirsgirêka gelê Kurdistanê li Rojhilata Navîn bi rêya aştî û diyalogê û bi awayekî serdemiyane bê çareserkirin. Her di wê hevdîtinê de birêz Serdar Yuksel rûmeta xwe ji bo rola dîrokî ya Serok Barzanî di azadîxwazî û xebata gelê Kurdistanê de û her wiha di şerê terorê û piştgirîkirina doza Kurd li Rojava de hebû, wê yekê jî xiste holê ku li Almanyayê û gelek cihên din ên cîhanê de xelk hene ku dost û piştgîr û hevxemê maf û daxwaziyên gelê Kurdistanê ne. Birêz Serdar Yuksel ezmûna Herêma Kurdistanê bilind û bi bihadar nirxand ku pêwîste piştgirî lê bê kirin. Her wiha rûmeta xwe ji bo rola Dezgeha Xêrxwaziya Barzanî jî hebû di alîkarî û hevkariya lêqewimiyan û koçber û penaberan de. Rewşa siyasî û dawî guhertinên li ser asta navçeyê û gefa terorê mijarên din ên wê hevdîtinê bûn.

author: Mekong Review 2
title: The cost of visibility Nathalie Chi
content:
Protests against the Chinese mega-embassy in London. Credit: Monkey Butler Images F ace covered, recognisable features hidden. A back-up phone in hand, location services disabled. No recent travel plans. No recent contact with family members in Tibet. Avoid cameras. Avoid interviews. At political protests against the Chinese government, including recent demonstrations against the planned Chinese mega-embassy in London, some Tibetan participants arrive with these calculations already made. Not everyone takes the same precautions, but everyone understands the necessity. Visibility travels, particularly for Tibetans. A single photograph, name, or online post can instantly cross borders, reaching far beyond the crowd standing on a London street. This landscape of fear has recently gained a physical anchor. In January 2026, the UK government approved China’s plan to redevelop the Royal Mint Court in central London into its largest diplomatic mission in Europe. The plan has faced sustained opposition from local residents, campaign groups, and politicians, who have raised concerns over national security, surveillance, protest safety, and the impact on surrounding areas. author: Benjamin Cordero
title: Ang Paglalayag sa Kawalan: Isang Pagsusuri sa The Odyssey (2026)
content:
Isang dambuhalang tagumpay sa sining ng pelikula ang The Odyssey (2026) ni Christopher Nolan. Bagaman napakamahal na ng halaga ng sine sa kasalukuyang panahon, isa itong biswal na hiyas na nararapat panoorin sa pinakamalaking telon hangga’t maaari. Ngunit sa ilalim ng nagngangalit na alon ng Dagat Mediteranyo o sa sindak na dulot ng Cyclops o sa bigat ng modernong pagganap na dala ni Matt Damon, may kuwentong pumipintig sa isang napakapamilyar na paraan.

Ang panonood ng The Odyssey sa pamamagitan ng matang Pilipino ay parang nakararanas ng matinding déjà vu . Para sa isang kulturang hinubog ng pangingibang-bansa, walang-katapusang pagtitiis, at pagkakawatak-watak ng pamilya, ang sampung taong pakikipagsapalaran ni Odysseus para lang makauwi ay hindi lang kuwento ng mitolohiyang Griyego—ito mismo ang buhay at kalagayan ng modernong Pilipino.

Ang pinakamabilis at pinakamatinding koneksyon ng pelikula ni Nolan sa buhay-Pilipino ay ang karakter mismo ni Odysseus. Siya ay isang lalaking nakakulong sa isang walang-awa at nakapapagod na pagpapatapon sa sarili. Sa pelikula, mariing ipinakita ni Nolan ang sikolohikal na epekto ng pagkakahiwalay ni Odysseus sa kanyang bayan; hindi lang siya lumalaban sa mga halimaw, kundi lumalaban din siya sa oras, sa distansya, at sa unti-unting paglaho ng alaala ng tahanang kanyang iniwan.

Ito ang salamin ng totoong buhay ng milyun-milyong Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs), ang ating mga bagong bayani. Katulad ni Odysseus na umalis ng Ithaca para lumaban sa digmaan sa Troy para sa kanyang bayan, ang OFW ay umaalis din sa Pilipinas para lumaban sa isang digmaang pang-ekonomiko sa dayuhang lupain. Pareho silang ginagabayan ng iisang layunin: ang buhayin, protektahan, at sa huli ay balikan ang pamilyang kanilang minamahal.

Kapag nakatulala si Odysseus (Matt Damon) sa karagatan habang nakakulong sa isla ng Ogygia, sinumang Pilipinong nanonood ay makikita ang mukha ng ating mga tita, tito, ina, at ama na nagpupuyat habang nakatingin sa bintana ng mga matataas na gusali sa Hong Kong, Dubai, o Singapore. Ang mga halimaw na hinarap ni Odysseus—ang mapanlinlang na akit ni Circe o ang nakaparalisang pagkalimot na dala ng mga Lotus-Eater—ay madaling maitumbas sa mga panganib ng pangingibang-bansa ngayon: (1) Ang tuksong makiangkop nang tuluyan sa dayuhang kultura at limutin ang sariling pinagmulan. (2) Ang mabigat at mapag-isang depresyon ng pagiging dayuhan sa ibang bansa at; (3) Ang mga burukrasya, kahirapan sa bayang babalikan at pisikal na hadlang na nagpapatagal sa pag-uwi nang maraming taon, o dekada.

Habang nakikipaglaban si Odysseus sa malalaking alon, ang bigat ng emosyon ng pelikula ay pasan naman nina Penelope (Anne Hathaway) at Telemachus (Tom Holland) sa Ithaca. Mahusay na ipinakita ni Nolan na ang Ithaca ay hindi isang marangyang kaharian na naghihintay sa kanilang hari, kundi isang gumuguhong bahay na kinatatawanan ng mga mapagsamantalang manliligaw/dayuhan na unti-unting nagpapasasa sa kanilang yaman.

Ang bahaging ito ng kuwento ay napakasakit tanggapin para sa mga pamilyang Pilipino. Kapag ang isang magulang ay umalis ng Pilipinas para magtrabaho sa abroad, ang pamilyang naiwan ay parang nakabinbin sa hangin. Si Penelope ang sumasalamin sa nakatutunaw at mapag-isang dusa ng asawang naiwan—na kadalasan ay ang ina na mag-isang nagtataguyod sa bahay, nagpoprotekta sa mga anak laban sa mga mapagsamantalang tao sa lipunan, at nagkukunwaring matatag kahit na nadudurog ang puso sa tindi ng pangungulila.

Si Telemachus naman ang kumakatawan sa “anak ng OFW.” Ipinakita ni Tom Holland ang isang binatang puno ng kumplikadong emosyon—may galit, may pangungulila, at may matinding pressure. Lumaki siya sa ilalim ng anino ng isang tanyag na ama na halos hindi niya matandaan, at napilitang ipagtanggol ang kanilang tahanan bago pa siya maging handa. Sa pang-araw-araw na buhay ng Pilipino, ito ang realidad ng milyun-milyong bata na lumalaki sa pamamagitan lamang ng video calls at remittance slips. Lumalaki silang walang ama o ina sa tabi, napipilitang magmatured nang maaga, nakalantad sa nauusong karahasan (maging sa sariling paaralan) at pasan ang bigat ng sakripisyo ng magulang habang nahihirapan ding kilalanin ang sarili.

Sa kaibuturan nito, ang The Odyssey ay isang paggalugad sa konsepto ng nostos—ang sinaunang salitang Griyego para sa pagbabalik-bayan. Sa kulturang Pilipino, ito ang ating pinakamalalim na mithiin: ang konsepto ng pagbabalik o pag-uwi.

author: Kevin Lin
title: The Seven Deadly Sins of Conferencing
content:
Many of us know from experience that the most memorable and enjoyable parts of participating in a conference are the tea and coffee breaks, the conversations lunches and dinners, the informal chats outside of the conference room while the meeting is still happening, and the late-night hangouts with other participants. Genuinely good conversations take place and relationships are formed or renewed in those moments. So why don’t we recognise what is obvious, and create structures that bring out these experiences?


Social movements rely on purposeful gatherings to connect, share experiences, and strategise. We do this so often we should be really good at it. But more often than not, things do not seem to quite work. This has prompted me to reflect, and then test my impressions with other conference-goers who turn out to be feeling much the same ways. I need to first acknowledge how much unseen labour goes into any event planning; the event organisers are the most invisible if everything goes well. But it is necessary to recognise and name things that do not seem to work.


Here are the seven deadly sins of conference organising. I want to speak to my fellow conference organisers: of course, not all of us committed all of the sins, and some of you have done much better. But many of the sins would sound familiar to us, and we often let our guards down. By naming them, we may do a better job at avoiding them, and get to organise and experience more effective, creative and joyful gatherings.


 


Greed


 


The first sin is greed. We are often greedy about what can be accomplished with a gathering, especially with sizable conferences. We want to invite many people to be there to meet and connect, while also want them to have substantial discussions.


A medium to large conference of dozens to a few hundred people is amazing. But it is not primarily a place for deep learning or for substantial conversations despite our best efforts and most sincere wishes. There are simply too many sessions, too many speakers and too many people to learn and engage deeply. We listen to one panel after another and hardly remember anything from each speaker, while facilitators apologise for running out of time and no more time for questions. We then try to have conversations during breaks that on average last for 5 to 10 minutes before rushing back to the next session or talking or introducing ourselves to someone else. You should not feel alone in experiencing this.


We know deep learning and substantial conversation are most likely to take place in much smaller meetings. You may really have to keep it to a very small number of participants, arguably no more than 10 or 15 but maybe even fewer, to have sustained conversations that give everyone time to think, allow ideas to develop, and for them to build on each other’s ideas.


The medium and large conferences serve other important goals: it is good for building new relationships or renewing old ones, for feeling part of a larger movement with many others with shared values and goals, and for experiencing the optimism and joy of movement-building. It is good enough to take away with you the connections you have made, a sense of the movement’s diversity and creativity, and the fact that people are doing the best they can under enormous pressure and risk.


If these are the realistic goals, then our task is to structure the events in ways that let people and ideas to breath, to have both structured discussions and unstructured time for spontaneous conversations, and to make these events into festivals.


 


Busyness


 


The second sin is busyness. Far too often, I have been in conference planning where the logistics – the venue search and booking, the travel arrangement, the drinks, snacks and meals, and the interpretation – take up most of the planning time. We end up spending very little time discussing and experimenting with the actual program. In fact, the program design at times feels like an afterthought.


The logistics discussions and preparations are often not completely done until the very last minute. Time for a program discussion tends to be squeezed in between logistics discussions. When we are tight on time, we tend to revert to the familiar and the safest: let us get these speakers speakers for these panels, and each speaks for 15 minutes. It is the least that can go wrong. No one can claim they love this, but we keep doing it anyway.

author: Rojava IC
title: Sleeper-Cell Report June 2026 – Justice Palace Department’s Head Killed
content:
The head of the Palace of Justice was seriously injured after being targeted in an attack on June 16. 


 


Key Points 


Five sleeper cell attacks were recorded in June; a slight increase from only three in May


A total of four military personnel were killed, and at least two injured 


Fatalities of two suspected ISIS affiliates were also recorded


Paper leaflets containing Pro-ISIS propaganda were distributed in several provinces throughout Syria


 


In Depth


This month, RIC recorded a total five attacks, two of which have been directly claimed by ISIS at the time of writing, the remaining three are believed to have been carried out by ISIS members.


On June 15, unidentified gunmen believed to be of an ISIS cell attacked the headquarters of general security forces, two of its members were killed and several others injured, west of Raqqa city, before one of the attackers self-detonated.  


On June 16, Salah Ahmad al-Saleh, head of the Palace of Justice in the town of Babila in rural Damascus was seriously injured by an explosive device attached to his vehicle. And on the same day, ISIS members targeted an oil tanker with machine-gun fire near the northern city of Manbij. Material damage to the tanker was reported.


On June 20, unidentified gunmen believed to be part of an ISIS cell, attacked members of the 76th Armored Division, causing the death of two Division’s members. The attack occurred near Tahnah junction in the western countryside of Manbij.


On June 24, two gunmen believed to be ISIS members, on a motorcycle opened fire on two members of the Engineering Regiment of the 72nd Division, on Ain Issa Road in Raqqa countryside, injuring both of them. 


On June 19, U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) forces conducted an airstrike in northwest Syria. CENTCOM confirmed the killing of Ali Husayn al-‘Ulaywi, a senior ISIS leader. 


Paper leaflets were distributed in several mosques across different areas in Daraa, Idlib and Aleppo provinces. The leaflets contain extremist content and rhetoric linked to ISIS.


Save the Children, an Australian children’s advocacy organization, called for the return of an ISIS-linked Australian woman and her disabled child from Syria after a failed repatriation attempt. Following the failed departure, Syrian authorities reportedly transferred them to a detention facility in northwestern Syria’s Idlib Governorate, since then, her family lost contact with her.


Another Australian woman was accused of supporting ISIS and appeared before a court in Melbourne, where prosecutors alleged she lived in a household that held a teenage girl in slavery while the victim was subjected to repeated abuse.  Her request for bail was rejected, as prosecutors argued she poses a risk to public safety. 


Tammy Bruce, U.S. Deputy Permanent Representative to the United Nations Ambassador said that it would continue working with Syria to combat ISIS, and support efforts to preserve stability and safety in the country.

author: Jules Arpula
title: Media hysteria shows high schoolers are right to protest Pauline Hanson
content:
There’s one thing I’ve learned organising the nationwide student walkout against Pauline Hanson, and it’s something they don’t tell you at school: If you’re a student protester, you cop more criticism from the establishment than if you’re a far-right politician who supports mass deportations and abortion bans.

Since we announced that we’re walking out of school on Thursday, there’s been a flood of hit pieces in the right-wing press, furious debates on talkback radio, and denunciations from politicians. The response just confirms why it’s so important for us to stand up—because the capitalist media and politicians aren’t going to. They’re up to their necks in complicity with Hanson’s rise, and they want to demonise anyone who has the guts to call her out.

The arguments against our strike are mind-bogglingly stupid. It’s funny to be lectured about staying in school by some of the dumbest people in Australia.

Liberal Party nepo-baby and 3AW shock-jock Tom Elliot, who graciously had me on his show, mused to his listeners: “Why underage students, who can’t even vote, are so worried about Pauline Hanson, I just don’t know”.

That’s a head-scratcher. We don’t enjoy even the very limited democratic rights afforded to adults, but we’re already seeing the way the rise of the far right is going to change our lives for the worse. We’ve been watching Trump’s rampage in the United States, as he’s slashed social services, threatened entire nations with annihilation and used immigration Gestapo thugs to terrorise and deport residents. We’ve watched as far-right riots have spread across the European continent and throughout Britain. But, according to Tom Elliot, what is there to worry about?

Plenty of journalists have said we need to stay in school and focus on our grades. Lucy Zelic asked in the

Daily Telegraph

, “With NAPLAN results sinking, why are we preaching Hanson hate in class?”

Let me spell it out. Hanson’s not going to put her racist rampage on pause until we all get our university degrees. The Victorian state election is in three months, and One Nation is building a far-right organisation to go out and win seats. She’s shaping politics right here, right now—putting migrant bashing, misogyny and attacks on workers at the centre of the discussion. If this is what we’re seeing already, what will it be like in five years when we’re entering the workforce?

The condescension echoes what we heard throughout the Palestine solidarity movement, when Premier Ben Carroll, who was then the education minister, warned us to leave politics up to our parents, and stay in school if we want to change the world.

These people clearly missed a few history lessons. Students have been central to movements for social change forever—from the high-schoolers who challenged segregation in the US South in the 1950s, to the heroic school kids who were massacred in the Soweto uprising in South Africa, to the role that school students have played across the world in the global Palestine solidarity movement. Those of us who have actually studied this history know you change the world by organising together, not by becoming soulless career politicians like Carroll.

In the

Herald Sun

, Andrew Bolt said that we are being “played” by socialist agitators, “extremists manipulating [us], with violence on their mind”.

High schoolers don’t need to be told what to think about Hanson. It’s pretty obvious that it’s racist to call for monoculture. It’s pretty obvious that it’s sexist to blame women for domestic violence. It’s pretty obvious that she’s backed by a coterie of rich creeps who want to roll back workers’ rights and line their pockets further.

I’m a member of the High School Anticapitalists in Melbourne, who identify Hanson as a hard-edged outgrowth of capitalist politics, in lockstep with the priorities of competition, nationalism and profit.

Although the high school walkout was initiated by High School Anticapitalists, it’s spread far and wide, to places where we have no members. Students from Bendigo to Geraldton to Tasmania are organising their own local walkouts, painting banners, and getting in touch with our group.

But it shouldn’t be surprising that socialists are behind the strike. The only political party that has wholeheartedly backed what we are doing in Melbourne is the Victorian Socialists. I think socialist politics is about standing on the right side of history, not cow-towing to what’s considered “reasonable” and …

author: Carissa Lee
title: MEDIA STATEMENT : FELIPE ALVAREZ CORONIAL INQUEST
content:
FELIPE ALVAREZ: FAMILY CALLS FOR ACCOUNTABILITY, TRANSPARENCY AND CORONIAL REFORM AFTER ACT CORONER’S FINDINGS


By Gabriela Alvarez-Sledge

Sister of the late Felipe Esteban Alvarez


Disclaimer: Readers please be advised this article mentions someone who has passed away.


“Felipe’s life mattered. His death mattered. What we learn from his death matters.”


The family of the late

Felipe Esteban Alvarez

 is calling for greater transparency, accountability and reform of the ACT coronial system following the release of the findings into his death.


Felipe died in March 2021 following an overdose at his Canberra residence.


Five years later, his family is still grieving while asking an important question:


What can be changed so that another family does not have to go through what ours has experienced?


Felipe was not simply a coronial file.


He was a brother, son, uncle and deeply loved member of his family.


His life had value.


His family believes his death deserved to be investigated as thoroughly, transparently and independently as possible.


WHAT THE CORONER FOUND


The findings of ACT Coroner Ken Archer identified serious concerns surrounding the circumstances of Felipe’s death.


The Coroner found that Felipe was experiencing a medical emergency and that emergency medical assistance was not sought for a significant period of time.


The Coroner found that the delay deprived Felipe of any chance of survival he may have had following his initial collapse.


The Coroner described the conduct of those present as

“morally blameworthy”

 and found that their conduct demonstrated a serious indifference to the possibility of loss of life.


The findings also identified broader public-safety concerns relating to the Canberra Alliance for Harm Minimisation and Advocacy (CAHMA), including concerns about governance, recruitment and screening, overdose-response training, naloxone availability and organisational accountability.


The Coroner found that appropriate screening and eligibility processes should have been applied to the relevant peer workers.


The findings also raised concerns about the organisation’s response following Felipe’s death and the need for stronger governance and accountability.


The Coroner recommended improvements to overdose-response training and stronger collaboration between harm-minimisation services, health agencies, ambulance services and police.


The family welcomes those recommendations.


THE FAMILY’S CONCERNS REMAIN


Throughout the coronial process, Felipe’s family provided information, documents and concerns about matters they believed were important to understanding what happened.


The family identified people who were present when Felipe suffered his overdose and sought to have the relevant evidence properly considered.


The family also provided written material that it believed was relevant to understanding what occurred.


However, the family remained concerned that not every matter it believed was important was fully tested or explored during the coronial process.


Because the Court has imposed restrictions concerning the publication of identities,

the family will not identify any person whose identity is subject to suppression

.


The family respects the Court’s orders.


There will be no naming of suppressed individuals in this statement.


The family’s concern has never been about publicly naming people.


It is about evidence.


It is about transparency.


It is about whether families can have confidence that every reasonable avenue of inquiry has been considered when their loved one dies.


THIS IS NOT AN ATTACK ON THE CORONER


The family wishes to make this position very clear.


Gabriela   Alvarez-Sledge is not seeking to undermine the independence of the Coroner or interfere with the findings.


She acknowledges the Coroner’s findings and welcomes the public-safety recommendations.


The family’s concern is about what can be learned from the entire experience.


A coronial system should not only determine how a person died.


It should also give bereaved families confidence that the investigation was thorough, transparent, fair and independent.


Where families continue to have genuine concerns about aspects of a coronial process, there should be an appropriate and independent pathway for those concerns to be considered.


A CALL FOR CORONIAL REFORM
