title: Kete: Special war policy targeting Dersim deepens through cultural genocide
content:
Dersim has for years remained one of the centres where the state's special war policies have been implemented most intensively. The drug networks targeting young people, the growth of gangs with impunity and the Gülistan Doku case, which has remained unresolved for more than six years, are regarded as consequences of the policies being pursued in the city. Those drawing attention to the deepening interventions targeting social memory and organised community life stress the importance of securing justice for Gülistan Doku and of a common struggle against special war policies.


Zeynel Kete, co-chair of the Democratic Alevi Association, spoke to ANF about the issue.


 


Dersim was the other of the monist nation-state conception


Zeynel Kete said that the concept of the “acceptable citizen” had been established from the founding of the state and that Dersim was excluded from this conception.


Noting that the nation-state conception shaped by the 1924 Constitution excluded Kurds and Alevis, Zeynel Kete said: “There is a 100-year-old state mentality. During the early period of the Republic's foundation, particularly with the process that began with the 1924 Constitution, the state defined its own respectable citizen. In making this definition, Kurds, Alevis and many other groups, including the Shafi'i sections of the Kurds, were not regarded as respectable citizens. Previously, a policy of control and supervision had likewise been pursued towards different ethnic groups and cultures, and efforts had essentially been made to eliminate them. When we look at the reports prepared about Dersim since the Ottoman period, we see that Dersim was always treated as a ‘boil’ that had to be subdued, conquered and eliminated. The reason is very clear. Dersim did not conform to the official ideology in terms of its ethnic structure, language, faith and culture. The official language was Turkish, and the dominant conception was the Turkish nation-state. But Dersim was not like that. Dersim had the Rêya Heq Alevi faith, a culture thousands of years old and a Kurdish identity. Therefore, from the perspective of the monist nation-state conception, Dersim was the other. Its language, culture, faith and ethnic structure did not correspond to the dominant conception. For this reason, it was considered necessary to bring it under control and supervision.”


Dersim’s women and sacred sites were targeted


Emphasising that the policies towards Dersim were not limited to physical interventions, Zeynel Kete said: “The reports on Dersim contained plans to intervene in Dersim's sacred sites, pirs, ocaks and community leaders. The Dersim reports also contained discourse that degraded Dersim's women and stripped them of their human dignity. This mentality of humiliation, destruction and devaluation can even be seen in the literature of the Republic's early period. This policy has continued to the present day. Dersim could not be subdued through the massacre in 1938. The state subsequently put policies of cultural genocide into effect.”


The beginning of cultural genocide


Zeynel Kete said that the policies towards Dersim had changed over time and that the concept of cultural genocide was implemented particularly through women and children:


“As we enter the second century of the Republic, Dersim was targeted in the Dersim Massacre that began in 1938, as one of the last strongholds of democratic society and a society based on consent against the capitalist modernist conception. Dersim is still not being internalised or accepted. Because truth is ancient in Dersim. It is not new. There is a search for truth that goes back thousands of years.


“When every individual in Dersim acknowledges their own historical truth, faith and culture, they also acknowledge their own free national values and their Kurdish identity. That is why they wanted to bring Dersim to its knees. But despite all the projects and physical destruction of the community, they could not subjugate Dersim.


“Then a new concept began: the concept of cultural genocide. As in the case of Sıdıka Avar, during the Dersim Massacre, young women and children from Dersim were taken to state-run orphanages in Elazığ, raised within the dominant Turkish culture and then sent to villages as elements of assimilation. The issue of Dersim's ‘lost girls’ is also part of this. There has been a policy specifically targeting women, and this policy has continued to the present day. However, the people …

title: Ocak: My mother never gave up, from Dersim to Galatasaray
content:
Emine Ocak, one of the leading figures of the Saturday Mothers' struggle for truth and justice and the mother of Hasan Ocak, a symbol of the victims of enforced disappearance in custody, was commemorated at the Human Rights Association (IHD) Istanbul Branch on the first anniversary of her death. Together with the family of Rıdvan Karakoç, who was also forcibly disappeared in custody, the Ocak family waged a long-running campaign against enforced disappearances that challenged the state's policies of uniformity and enforced silence, racism disguised as nationalism, labor exploitation, torture, massacres and what they described as the state's fascist character. Emine Ocak, who survived the Dersim Massacre and later devoted her life to the struggle for truth and justice, went on to lead years of civil disobedience protests in Galatasaray Square after her son was forcibly disappeared in Istanbul. Hüseyin Ocak spoke to ANF about the life and legacy of his 90-year-old mother.


My mother was just 18 months old during the Dersim Massacre


Hüseyin Ocak said his mother, Emine Ocak, had lived through massacres, repression and resistance from the very beginning of her life. He said she was born in the village of Xaltan, in Nazimiye, Dersim, and that when the Dersim Massacre began in 1937, her family fled into the surrounding mountains to escape the military.


He said his mother and her twin sister, Sevgi, were only 18 months old at the time. Ocak said: "While the family was hiding in the forest, they feared the babies' cries would reveal their location. They even considered killing my mother and her twin sister. They said, 'They will find us here and kill us all. Rather than all of us dying, let's kill these two children.' My grandmother refused. She said, 'I will take the children somewhere else. If they find anyone, let them find us and kill us. You survive.' She took my mother and her twin sister and hid in the opposite direction from where the rest of the family was sheltering. At that time, soldiers were burning villages and shooting villagers they came across. When my grandmother returned to the village with the two babies, she found it burned to the ground and saw that my mother's two uncles had been killed there. She then tried to rebuild her life. What I mean is that my mother faced the threat of death from the very moment she opened her eyes to the world."


We became targets of fascists in Elazığ


Ocak said his mother and her family moved to the village of Çukur in central Dersim in 1943. He said she married his father, who had also moved there from Nazimiye, when she was just 15 or 16 years old. Ocak also said: "In 1973, my parents moved to Elazığ (Xarpêt), where they once again became targets, this time of fascists. I was 10 years old then. We were fighting for our lives. It was one of the most violent periods, and we lived with the fear that our home could be bombed at any moment. Fascists repeatedly attacked us, and we were detained many times because of the events taking place there. My brother Ali Ocak lost his hearing as a result of torture. Our lives were always marked by hardship. My brother Hasan Ocak, who was later forcibly disappeared in custody, also witnessed those difficult years. He completed primary school, secondary school and high school in Elazığ, then enrolled at the Siirt Education Institute. After graduating, he moved to Istanbul in 1985."


Ocak said the family was also forced to leave Elazığ after the 12 September 1980 military coup and added: "We were a well-known family and were constantly under threat. I was the first to move to Istanbul as a university student. Later, my brothers Ali and Hasan joined me. In 1987, we brought the entire family to Istanbul. But we never found peace there either. Hasan was forcibly disappeared in custody ten years after arriving in Istanbul."


Hasan's last stop was my shop


Ocak said the last person Hasan spoke to before his detention was their mother by phone, and that he later stopped by his shop. He added: "At the time, I was running a shop in Laleli. Hasan came by, and we planned to meet again at home that evening. But after he left my shop, he never came home. It was Newroz on 21 March, and many people were being detained and arrested. We believe Hasan was taken into custody somewhere between Aksaray and Topkapı, because we were living in Avcılar. title: Fenerbahçe Lukaku ile anlaştı: Gözler bonservis pazarlığında
content:
Fotoğraf: Илья Хохлов/Wikimedia Commons CC BY-SA 3.0

Fenerbahçe, yeni sezon öncesi hücum hattını güçlendirmek için forvet arayışlarını sürdürüyor. Sarı-lacivertliler, Napoli forması giyen Belçikalı golcü Romelu Lukaku ile prensip anlaşmasına vardı.

Kulüp ile oyuncu arasındaki görüşmelerin olumlu sonuçlandığı, transferin önündeki temel engelin ise Napoli ile bonservis konusunda anlaşma sağlanması olduğu belirtildi.

Fenerbahçe, Lukaku’nun transferi için Napoli’ye 6 milyon euroluk bonservis teklifi sundu. İtalyan kulübünün bu teklifi kabul etmediği ve taraflar arasındaki görüşmelerin sürdüğü bildirildi.

Sarı-lacivertli yönetimin, Napoli ile bonservis bedeli konusunda yeni bir teklif üzerinden pazarlık yapması bekleniyor.

Fenerbahçe yönetimi, Lukaku transferinin gerçekleşmemesi ihtimaline karşı alternatif isimlerle de temaslarını sürdürüyor.

Borussia Dortmund forması giyen Serhou Guirassy ile Aston Villa’nın golcüsü Ollie Watkins, sarı-lacivertlilerin transfer listesinde bulunuyor.

Yönetimin, bu iki oyuncudan biri için uygun mali koşullar oluşması halinde transfer planında değişikliğe gidebileceği belirtiliyor.

title: Vize serbestisi için önemli adım: 6 kriterle ilgili çalışma başlatıldı
content:
Fotoğraf: https://kaboompics.com//Pexels

Avrupa Komisyonu'nun 2025 Schengen vize istatistiklerine göre Türkiye'den yapılan başvurular yüzde 8 artarak 1,26 milyonu aşarken ret oranı yüzde 14,6 seviyesinde kaldı. Türk vatandaşlarına en yüksek ret oranı uygulayan ülkeler şöyle sıralandı:

Cumhurbaşkanı Yardımcısı Cevdet Yılmaz, Türkiye'nin Avrupa Birliği ile yürüttüğü vize serbestisi uygulamasında kalan 6 kriter için çalışma başlatıldığını açıkladı. Yılmaz, Avrupa'daki siyasi iradeyi de görmek istediklerini belirterek; "Kişisel verilerin korunması en önemli maddelerden biri bu. Geri kabul ve terör tanımı ile ilgili bir mesele var. KVKK konusunda Adalet Bakanlığımıza teşekkür ediyorum. Akın Bakanımız, bir bilim kurulu oluşturdu, çalışma yürüttü, ben de koordine ediyorum. Dışişleri, Adalet, İçişleri bütün bakanlıklarımızı bir araya getirdik, toplantılar yaptık. O kurulda bu kanun tartışıldı. Bu biraz mutfak çalışmasıydı. Burada yeni bir yaklaşım geliştirildi. Kurumlarımız tarafından şimdi Dışişleri Bakanlığımız üzerinden Avrupa kurumları ile istişareler yapılacak" dedi.

Türkiye, AB ile yürüttüğü vize serbestisi uygulamasında 6 kritere takıldı. 13 yıldır sağlanamayan kriterler şu şekilde:

- Terörle mücadele yasasında değişiklik,

- AB Polis Örgütü (Europol) ile operasyonel işbirliği anlaşması imzalanması,

- Avrupa Konseyi bünyesindeki Yolsuzluğa Karşı Devletler Grubu'nun (GRECO) yolsuzlukla mücadele alanındaki önerilerinin uygulanması,

- Kişisel verilere yönelik yasal düzenlemelerin Avrupa standartlarıyla uyumlu hale getirilmesi,

- Suç bağlantılı konularda tüm AB üyeleriyle işbirliğine gidilmesi,

- Türkiye üzerinden kural dışı şekilde AB ülkelerine geçiş yapan kişilerin geri alınmasına ilişkin Geri Kabul Anlaşması'nın (GKA) tüm unsurlarıyla uygulanması.

Çerçeve yasanın TBMM Adalet Komisyonu'ndan geçmesi ardından terörle mücadele ve vize serbestisi konusunu değerlendiren Cumhurbaşkanı Yardımcısı Yılmaz, Türkiye'nin Avrupa Birliği'yle (AB) yürüttüğü vize serbestisi uygulamasında kalan 6 kriter konusunda bir çalışma başlattığını duyurdu.

"Kişisel verilerin korunması en önemli maddelerden biri bu. Geri kabul ve terör tanımı ile ilgili bir mesele var. KVKK konusunda Adalet Bakanlığımıza teşekkür ediyorum. Akın Bakanımız, bir bilim kurulu oluşturdu, çalışma yürüttü, ben de koordine ediyorum. Dışişleri, Adalet, İçişleri bütün bakanlıklarımızı bir araya getirdik, toplantılar yaptık. O kurulda bu kanun tartışıldı. Bu biraz mutfak çalışmasıydı. Burada yeni bir yaklaşım geliştirildi. Kurumlarımız tarafından şimdi Dışişleri Bakanlığımız üzerinden Avrupa kurumları ile istişareler yapılacak. Bu konuda bizim Avrupa'daki siyasi iradeyi görmemiz lazım, onların da atması gereken adımlar var."

title: Kayseri'de ölümlü kavga: Biber gazı sıkıp bıçakladılar
content:
Olay, saat 01.00 sıralarında Kocasinan ilçesine bağlı Sahabiye Mahallesi Yıldırım Caddesi’nde meydana geldi.

İddiaya göre, iki grup arasında henüz belirlenemeyen nedenle başlayan tartışma kısa sürede kavgaya dönüştü. Kavga sırasında bir grup, S.M. ve N.M.’ye biber gazı sıktıktan sonra bıçakla saldırdı.

Çevredekilerin ihbarı üzerine olay yerine polis ve sağlık ekipleri sevk edildi.

Yaralanan S.M. ve N.M., sağlık ekiplerinin olay yerindeki ilk müdahalesinin ardından ambulanslarla hastaneye kaldırıldı.

Ağır yaralanan S.M., doktorların tüm müdahalesine rağmen hayatını kaybetti. N.M.’nin tedavisinin sürdüğü bildirildi.

Polis ekipleri, kavganın ardından olay yerinden kaçan şüphelilerin yakalanması için çalışma başlattı.

Olayla ilgili soruşturma sürüyor.
